newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Hooded gunmen slay 10 woodcutters in NW Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Hooded gunmen slay 10 woodcutters in NW Colombia.

text.p: A gang of hooded gunmen dressed in black massacred 10 woodcutters in northwest Colombia -- the latest in a wave of mass murders across the north and east of the country -- police said on Friday.
The attack by a suspected right-wing death squad took place in a rural area near the town of Retiro, in war-torn Antioquia province, late on Thursday. Three children survived, the town mayor said.
"Eight men wearing black clothes and hoods carried out this attack," Antioquia police chief Col. Luis Eduardo Garcia said. "Nine people were killed instantly a tenth died later in hospital."
Police sources said the killers appeared to be paramilitary fighters judging by the way they were dressed.

The timber trade is the linchpin of the local economy around Retiro. All the dead, aged between 17 and 56, had come from surrounding communities to fell pine and cypress trees, Mayor Leon Cartagena told Reuters.
He said all the victims had been shot in the back of the head with pistols but declined to speculate on who may have been behind the attack.

Scores of peasants have been massacred across northern and eastern Colombia this year as guerrillas and paramilitary gangs battle for control of the countryside ahead of municipal and provincial elections in October.

The army has been unable to stem the escalation in violence, complaining of lack of manpower and equipment, leading political analysts to suggest the government will soon be forced to declare a state of "internal disorder" to enable it to decree new strong-arm laws to combat the growing threat of the irregular armed groups.
